content: The metabolism of eluxadoline may be affected when co-administered with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors such as omeprazole and encorafenib. Encorafenib can both inhibit and induce CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations, potentially leading to increased toxicity or reduced efficacy of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of ephedrine through passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. It also increases the levels of erythromycin base, erythromycin ethylsuccinate, erythromycin lactobionate, and erythromycin stearate through unknown mechanisms. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of escitalopram by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Similarly, eslicarbazepine acetate increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of esmolol and etidronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. Etravirine increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Fedratinib increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments for CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are advised. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Co-administration with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase adverse effects of flibanserin. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Fluconazole increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. Sodium bicarbonate also decreases fosamprenavir levels through the same mechanism. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of fosinopril through an unspecified mechanism. Omeprazole levels are decreased by fosphenytoin, phenobarbital, and phenytoin through effects on CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of gabapentin, gabapentin enacarbil, and ibandronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. Omeprazole decreases the levels of gefitinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) if possible. If necessary, separate doses by 12 hours. Sodium bicarbonate increases the levels of glipizide and glyburide by increasing gastric pH. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of isoniazid, itraconazole, ketoconazole, and labetalol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. Omeprazole increases the levels of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of levoketoconazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. Omeprazole increases lomitapide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor is a strong CYP3A4 inducer and may also induce or inhibit CYP2C19 and P-gp. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Sodium bicarbonate increases memantine levels through passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Omeprazole increases methotrexate levels by decreasing renal clearance. Temporary withdrawal of PPIs may be considered in some patients. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of methscopolamine, metoprolol, and nadolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. Omeprazole decreases the effects of methylphenidate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. For extended-release methylphenidate capsules, consider separating administration from antacids or acid suppressants. Sodium bicarbonate increases mexiletine levels through passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Omeprazole increases midazolam intranasal levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with mild CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Modafinil increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of moexipril through an unspecified mechanism. Omeprazole decreases mycophenolate levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies to mycophenolate mofetil but is less significant for enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of nebivolol, nitrofurantoin, and omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. Omeprazole increases oxcarbazepine levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of pamidronate, penbutolol, and penicillamine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. Pentobarbital decreases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of perindopril through an unspecified mechanism. Phenobarbital and phenytoin decrease omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sodium bicarbonate decreases the levels of pindolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. Omeprazole decreases the levels of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
